mainTopic: The rules of תרומת מעשר and early-taken מעשר ראשון, and the difference between 'finished work' for מעשר and forbidden labor on שבת and יום טוב.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a derivation: just as תרומה גדולה is taken only from finished produce at the granary and winepress, so is תרומת מעשר. The גמרא asks why the source says 'מחשב' (calculates) when תרומת מעשר is a fixed tenth. It answers that the source follows אבא אלעזר בן גימל, who allows both תרומות to be separated by estimate and by thought. Next, רבי שמעון בן לקיש teaches two rules about מעשר ראשון taken early, while the grain is still on the stalks. It is still obligated in תרומת מעשר, but it is exempt from תרומה גדולה. אביי explains that grain in a pile has already become דגן, while grain on the stalks has not. The גמרא then quotes a משנה about peeling barley and רבי אלעזר's comment 'וכן לשבת'. Because of the practice of רב and רבי חייא, it moves his comment to the wheat clause. This leads to the principle that שבת forbids only מלאכת מחשבת, so piling or gathering produce can finish it for מעשר and still be permitted on שבת. Finally, the גמרא asks how one may rub and blow grain in a changed way on יום טוב, and רב's answer about blowing continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both תרומות are taken only from finished produce
steps.stepSummary: The end of a derivation from the פסוק: just as תרומה גדולה is taken only from the granary and the winepress, so is תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...only from the granary and the winepress. So too, תרומת מעשר is separated only from the granary and the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the פסוק that began on the previous amud. It compares תרומת מעשר to תרומה גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'כדגן מן הגורן וכמלאה מן היקב' is read as putting the two terumos side by side. So the rule for תרומה גדולה, that it applies only to processed produce at the granary or winepress, also applies to תרומת מעשר. This comparison is what makes the next question possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Granary or threshing floor, where grain is processed and piled
Winepress, or the vat where wine collects
The tenth of the מעשר ראשון that the לוי gives to the כהן
The first gift taken from produce for the כהן; the Torah sets no fixed amount

phrases.english: only from the granary and from the winepress,
phrases.notes: End of the first half of the comparison, which describes תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: so too, teruma of the tithe is not separated
except from the granary and from the winepress.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינָהּ נִיטֶּלֶת אֶלָּא מִן הַגּוֹרֶן וּמִן הַיֶּקֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That תרומת מעשר follows the same rules as תרומה גדולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ונחשב לכם תרומתכם כדגן מן הגורן וכמלאה מן היקב' (במדבר יח:כז)

steps.title: Why say 'calculates' if a tenth needs exact measuring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'מחשב': תרומת מעשר is a fixed tenth, so it should require measuring, not estimating.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Calculates'? It should need measuring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a challenge on the wording of the source. If we are dealing with תרומת מעשר, why does it use the word 'calculates'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה גדולה has no fixed Torah amount, so estimating it makes sense. תרומת מעשר is exactly one tenth of the מעשר, so it seems it must be measured precisely. The word 'מחשב' therefore seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: Calculates or estimates; separating by estimate or by thought
Exact measuring
It requires, it needs

phrases.english: Calculates?
phrases.notes: Quoting the word in the source being discussed.

phrases.english: But it requires measuring!
phrases.notes: A fixed tenth needs exact measurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is identified as תרומת מעשר, the גמרא attacks the word 'מחשב'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת מעשר is a fixed tenth, which requires measuring. Estimating fits only תרומה גדולה.

steps.title: The source follows אבא אלעזר בן גימל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source follows the view of אבא אלעזר בן גימל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is אבא אלעזר בן גימל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming the תנא whose view the source follows. The next step brings the ברייתא that proves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question of step 2 assumed everyone agrees that תרומת מעשר must be measured. The answer shows that one תנא holds otherwise. So the word 'מחשב' is correct according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A formula for identifying the author of a source
A תנא quoted in the ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַנִּי אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גִּימֶל הִיא,
phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Abba Elazar ben Gimmel,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גִּימֶל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought תרומת מעשר always requires exact measuring, so 'מחשב' is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אבא אלעזר בן גימל, תרומת מעשר may also be separated by estimation, so 'מחשב' is correct.

steps.title: The ברייתא: both תרומות can be separated by estimate and thought
steps.stepSummary: אבא אלעזר בן גימל reads 'ונחשב לכם תרומתכם' as covering both terumos, so both may be separated by estimation and by thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: אבא אלעזר בן גימל says: 'And your teruma shall be reckoned to you.' The פסוק speaks of two terumos, תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר. Just as תרומה גדולה is separated by estimate and by thought, so too תרומת מעשר is separated by estimate and by thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows the opinion of אבא אלעזר בן גימל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'תרומתכם' (your terumos) as including both kinds of teruma. The word 'ונחשב' (reckoned) teaches that estimating, or even just intending in one's mind, is enough. Because the פסוק joins the two terumos, תרומת מעשר gets the same lenient method as תרומה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
And it shall be reckoned or considered
Estimation by eye
Thought; separating by intention alone

steps.whatToRemember: According to אבא אלעזר בן גימל, the פסוק 'ונחשב לכם תרומתכם' allows תרומת מעשר, like תרומה גדולה, to be separated by estimate and by thought. That is why the source can say 'מחשב'.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גִּימֶל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Abba Elazar ben Gimmel says:
"And your teruma shall be reckoned to you" —
the verse speaks of two terumot,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: one is teruma gedola and one is teruma of the tithe.
Just as teruma gedola is separated
by estimation and by thought —
so too, teruma of the tithe is separated
by estimation and by thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גִּימֶל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That according to אבא אלעזר בן גימל, תרומת מעשר may be separated by estimation
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'ונחשב לכם תרומתכם' as referring to both terumos

steps.title: מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks is still obligated in תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a statement mentioned earlier. רבי אבהו quotes רבי שמעון בן לקיש: מעשר ראשון taken early, on the stalks, carries an obligation of תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: מעשר ראשון that the לוי took early, while the grain was still on the stalks, has a name that makes it טבל until תרומת מעשר is taken from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section to study a statement that was quoted earlier only in passing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the לוי took his מעשר before the כהן's תרומה גדולה was separated, while the grain was still on the stalks. Even so, that מעשר becomes טבל and is forbidden until תרומת מעשר is separated from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; returning to examine a statement quoted earlier
The first tithe, given to the לוי
He took it early, before the תרומה גדולה
Stalks or ears of grain, before threshing
Makes it טבל, forbidden until the required gift is separated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terumos. מעשר taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה, as רבי שמעון בן לקיש rules in step 8. This statement says it is still obligated in תרומת מעשר. These two rules do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: Returning to a statement quoted earlier in passing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
first tithe that he took early, while on the stalks —
phrases.notes: The לוי took it before the כהן received תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: its name makes it tevel with regard to teruma of the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section analyzing a statement mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון taken early on the stalks is טבל until תרומת מעשר is taken from it.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this early מעשר should be obligated in תרומת מעשר. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was taken at the stalk stage, before the produce was finished. So one might think no obligation applies to it yet. The גמרא wants the logic behind the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why early מעשר taken on the stalks is obligated in תרומת מעשר

steps.title: Because it carries the name 'מעשר'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains: since the name מעשר has taken effect on it, the obligation of תרומת מעשר follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since the name 'מעשר' has taken effect on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once this produce is called 'מעשר', it has the status of מעשר. Every מעשר ראשון must have תרומת מעשר taken from it, so this one must too. Taking it early on the stalks changes when it was taken, but not its status as מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
The name has taken effect on it; it has received that status

steps.whatToRemember: Early מעשר taken on the stalks still requires תרומת מעשר, because it has the name 'מעשר'.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since the name of tithe has gone out upon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא עָלָיו שֵׁם מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since it is called 'מעשר', the obligation of תרומת מעשר applies to it.

steps.title: Tithe taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש rules that מעשר ראשון separated early, while the grain is still on the stalks, is פטור from תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: First tithe that was separated early, while the grain was still on the stalks, is exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי שמעון בן לקיש about a tithe that was taken out of order, before the תרומה גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal order is: first the כהן gets תרומה גדולה, then the לוי gets מעשר ראשון. Here the לוי 'jumped ahead' and took his tithe while the grain was still on the stalks. That tithe should really have had some תרומה גדולה in it, but רבי שמעון בן לקיש says the לוי does not have to give that part to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe: one tenth of the crop, given to the לוי
That he took it early, ahead of the proper order
Stalks: grain that is not yet threshed
The 'big terumah': the first gift from the crop, given to the כהן
Exempt, not obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 5. There, רבי שמעון בן לקיש said this early tithe IS obligated in תרומת מעשר, the לוי's own tenth. Here he says it is EXEMPT from תרומה גדולה, the כהן's first gift. These are two different terumos.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole discussion that follows: why taking the tithe early can cancel the כהן's share.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
First tithe that he separated early, while still on the stalks —
phrases.notes: The לוי received his tithe before the כהן received תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: is exempt from the great terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related second ruling by the same אמורא about tithe taken early on the stalks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון separated on the stalks before תרומה גדולה is exempt from תרומה גדולה.

steps.title: The verse source: only a tithe from the tithe
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'מעשר מן המעשר' shows that from the לוי's tithe you take only תרומת מעשר, and not also תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And you shall set apart from it a תרומה for ה׳, a tithe from the tithe.' This means: I told you to take a tithe from the tithe, and not both תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר from the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the Torah source for רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the לוי to give 'a tenth of the tithe', which is תרומת מעשר. The דיוק is that this is the only gift owed from the מעשר. So the לוי does not owe תרומה גדולה on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
And you shall set apart
A tithe from the tithe: one tenth of the לוי's tithe
The terumah of the tithe, which the לוי gives to the כהן

phrases.english: As it is said: "And you shall set apart from it a terumah for ה׳,
a tithe from the tithe" (Bamidbar 18:26),
"A tithe from the tithe" I told you,
phrases.notes: ה׳ is speaking: this is the only gift I required from the tithe.

phrases.english: and not both the great terumah and the terumah of the tithe
from the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for the rule in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The exemption of early-separated מעשר ראשון from תרומה גדולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 18:26, 'מעשר מן המעשר', read as limiting the gift owed from the tithe to תרומת מעשר alone.

steps.title: Then even tithe taken from the pile should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if the פסוק exempts the tithe, then even tithe separated early from the finished pile (כרי) should be exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, then even if he took it early from the pile, it should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the rule. The reason seems too broad, so why limit it to the stalks?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מעשר מן המעשר' says nothing about stalks or piles. So if it exempts the tithe, it should also exempt a tithe taken after threshing, from the pile. But we know that in that case the tithe is obligated in תרומה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from the previous logic)
A pile of threshed, finished grain
Also

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If so,
even if he separated it early from the pile, it should also be exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּימוֹ בִּכְרִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation of Step 9 for proving too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from 'מעשר מן המעשר' as the basis for the exemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק makes no difference between stalks and pile. So it should exempt early tithe from the pile as well, which is not the halacha.

steps.title: A second verse obligates the tithe in תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that for the pile case, a different פסוק, 'מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו את כל תרומת ה׳', requires תרומה גדולה even from the tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: About your question, the verse says: 'From all your tithes you shall set apart all of ה׳'s תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא: there is a second פסוק that makes the tithe obligated in תרומה גדולה, and that פסוק covers the pile case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All of ה׳'s terumah' includes תרומה גדולה, and it must be taken 'from all your tithes'. So there are two פסוקים pulling in opposite directions. One exempts the tithe and one obligates it. Each must apply to a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: About you, regarding your question
The פסוק says
From all your tithes

phrases.english: He said to him: About your case the verse says:
"From all your tithes you shall set apart
phrases.notes: The word in parentheses is a textual variant. The פסוק (במדבר 18:29) reads 'מתנתיכם', 'your gifts'.

phrases.english: all of ה׳'s terumah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge with a second, opposing פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second verse that covers the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'מעשר מן המעשר' alone would exempt every early tithe, even from the pile.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second פסוק obligates the tithe in תרומה גדולה, so the exemption applies only to the stalks and the obligation applies to the pile.

steps.title: Why assign each verse to its case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason we have to apply the obligating פסוק to the pile and the exempting פסוק to the stalks, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind splitting the two פסוקים this way. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we have two opposite פסוקים, we need a reason for which case gets which פסוק. Without a reason, the split could just as well be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? Asks for the reason behind a choice

phrases.english: And what did you see (to divide it this way)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distribution of the two פסוקים set up in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the obligating פסוק goes to the pile and the exempting פסוק goes to the stalks.

steps.title: Pile grain is finished grain, stalk grain is not
steps.stepSummary: Grain in a pile has become finished grain (אידגן), so the תרומה גדולה obligation already took hold. Grain on the stalks has not, so the tithe was taken before any obligation existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the pile) has become grain, and that one (the stalks) has not become grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the split: the obligation of תרומה גדולה only starts once the grain is finished and piled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the stalks, the grain is not yet 'grain' (דגן), so there is no תרומה גדולה obligation yet. Once it is called מעשר, the chance to take תרומה from it is lost. In the pile, the obligation already took effect, so calling it מעשר cannot erase it.

keyTerms.meaning: This one
It has become grain: fully processed, so the terumah obligation applies
It has not yet become grain

steps.whatToRemember: Early tithe taken on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה, based on 'מעשר מן המעשר'. Early tithe taken from the pile is obligated, based on 'מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו'. The difference is whether the grain had already become דגן when it was named מעשר.

phrases.english: This one (in the pile) has become grain,
and that one (on the stalks) has not become grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 and closes the discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The terumah obligation starts only when the grain becomes דגן, finished and piled. In the pile it already started. On the stalks it had not, so the tithe escapes it.

steps.title: The משנה on peeling barley, and רבי אלעזר's comparison to שבת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מעשרות rules that peeling barley one grain at a time and eating is exempt from מעשר, but peeling into one's hand creates an obligation. רבי אלעזר says the same rule applies to שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: One who peels barley may peel one at a time and eat. But if he peeled and put them into his hand, he is obligated. רבי אלעזר said: and the same is true for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about snacking on barley, plus רבי אלעזר's comment that the same rule works for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating grain by grain is casual snacking, so the food is not yet 'finished' and no מעשר is due. Collecting a handful makes it a real processed amount, so it is obligated. רבי אלעזר applies this to שבת: one at a time is allowed, but a handful counts as forbidden threshing.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
One who peels
Barley
Obligated (here, in מעשר)
And the same applies to שבת

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
One who peels barley,
may peel one at a time and eat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קִלֵּף וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: But if he peeled and put them into his hand, he is obligated (in tithes).
Rabbi Elazar said: And the same applies to Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about what counts as 'finished processing' for מעשר and for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Peeling barley one by one is exempt; a handful is obligated in מעשר. רבי אלעזר says the same line applies to שבת.

steps.title: רב and רבי חייא had barley peeled by the cupful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: the wives of רב and רבי חייא peeled barley for them by the cupful on שבת, so a large amount cannot be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב's wife would peel for him cup after cup! And רבי חייא's wife would peel for him cup after cup!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's comparison to שבת, using the real practice of two great sages, רב and רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If peeling a handful of barley were forbidden threshing on שבת, רב and רבי חייא would never have allowed whole cupfuls to be peeled for them. Their practice shows that peeling barley, even in quantity, is permitted on שבת. That contradicts רבי אלעזר's 'the same applies to שבת' for the barley clause.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
His wife
Cupful after cupful

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rav's wife would peel (barley) for him
by the cupful!
And Rabbi Chiya's wife would peel for him
by the cupful!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב מְקַלְּפָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ כָּסֵי כָּסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's statement from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the barley rule also applies to שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The actual practice of רב and רבי חייא shows that peeling barley in large amounts is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's comment was said on the wheat clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's comment was said on the later clause of the משנה, about rubbing wheat and blowing away the chaff.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said on the later clause: One who rubs ears of wheat may blow away the chaff a little at a time and eat. But if he blew and put them into his lap, he is obligated. רבי אלעזר said: and the same is true for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by moving רבי אלעזר's 'the same applies to שבת' off the barley clause and onto the wheat clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley peeling is now left without any שבת prohibition, which fits what רב and רבי חייא did. Rubbing wheat and blowing off the chaff is closer to real threshing and winnowing. So for wheat, a lapful counts as forbidden work on שבת, just as it creates an obligation in מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said on the later clause
One who rubs (ears of grain) by hand
Ears of grain that are rubbed to free the kernels
Blows (to remove the chaff)
His lap

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אלעזר changed his opinion. The גמרא is only correcting which clause of the משנה his short comment was attached to.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
it was stated on the latter clause:
One who rubs ears of wheat,

phrases.aramaic: מְנַפֵּחַ עַל יָד עַל יָד וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: may blow (off the chaff) little by little and eat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נִפַּח וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ חֵיקוֹ — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: But if he blew and put them into his lap, he is obligated.
Rabbi Elazar said: And the same applies to Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 15 by moving רבי אלעזר's comment to a different clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocation of an אמורא's statement to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's comment was on the barley clause, which would forbid peeling a handful of barley on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: His comment was on the wheat clause. Peeling barley on שבת is permitted even in large amounts.

steps.title: Can something be finished work for מעשר but not for שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל objects: by this reading, a handful of barley is 'finished' for מעשר but not for שבת. But שבת is stricter, so how can that be?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל objected: And in the first clause, is it 'yes' for מעשר and 'no' for שבת? Is there anything that does not count as finishing the work for שבת, yet does count as finishing the work for מעשר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges the answer from Step 16 by pointing to the odd result it leaves in the barley clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After Step 16, the barley clause makes a handful obligated in מעשר but leaves it permitted on שבת. רבי אבא בר ממל assumes שבת is always at least as strict as מעשר. So whatever counts as completed work for מעשר should also count as completed work for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objected to it
The first clause
Completion of the work (the point where processing is finished)
Is there anything at all...?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel strongly objected:
And the first clause: for tithes yes, for Shabbat no?
Is there anything that regarding Shabbat
is not the completion of the work,
yet regarding tithes it is the completion of the work?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of the answer in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that puts רבי אלעזר's comment only on the wheat clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It creates a case that is 'finished' for מעשר but not for שבת, which seems impossible because שבת is stricter.

steps.title: Piling produce: finished for מעשר but permitted on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rejects רבי אבא בר ממל's assumption. Making a pile (העמדת ערמה) is the 'finishing point' for מעשר for some vegetables, yet on שבת piling is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי objected: And is there no such case? But there is 'their threshing floor' for מעשר! As we learned: What is their threshing floor for מעשר? Cucumbers and gourds, from when he trims off their fuzz; and if he does not trim them, from when he makes a pile. And we also learned about onions: from when he makes a pile. Yet regarding שבת, making a pile is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי knocks down the assumption behind Step 17 by showing a real case where something is finished work for מעשר but not for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For cucumbers, gourds, and onions, the משנה says that stacking them into a pile is what makes them 'finished' and obligated in מעשר. Gathering produce into a pile is not one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת, so it is פטור there. This shows that מעשר and שבת use different standards, so the barley clause in Step 16 is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Their 'threshing floor' for מעשר: the point at which produce becomes obligated
Cucumbers
Gourds
From when they trim off the fuzz
Stacking produce into a pile
Exempt (not a forbidden מלאכה)

steps.whatToRemember: What counts as 'finished work' for מעשר is not always the same as for שבת. Piling produce finishes it for מעשר, but piling is not a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. So רבי אלעזר's comment can apply to wheat only, and barley peeling stays permitted on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that מעשר is set by when produce looks 'ready', while שבת is set by the defined list of מלאכות. They are two separate systems.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, strongly objected:
And is there not? But there is 'their threshing floor' for tithes,
as we learned: What is their threshing floor for tithes?
Cucumbers and gourds: from when they are trimmed of their fuzz.
And those not trimmed: from when he makes a pile.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי בְצָלִים — מִשֶּׁיַּעֲמִיד עֲרֵמָה.
phrases.english: And we also learned about onions: from when he makes a pile.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ גַּבֵּי שַׁבָּת — הַעֲמָדַת עֲרֵמָה פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Whereas regarding Shabbat, making a pile is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: וְלָא, וְהָא גׇּרְנָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind רבי אבא בר ממל's objection in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The premise that anything finished for מעשר must also be finished for שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Piling produce is a counterexample: it fixes the מעשר obligation, but it is פטור on שבת.

steps.title: The Torah forbids only purposeful creative labor on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת completes his rejection. Piling is פטור on שבת because the Torah forbids only מלאכת מחשבת. The same reason applies to collecting peeled barley in one's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say about piling? The Torah forbade only planned, creative labor. Here too, the Torah forbade only planned, creative labor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his answer. He explains why piling is allowed on שבת and applies the same reason to gathering peeled barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא בר ממל assumed that anything counted as 'finished' for מעשר must also be forbidden on שבת. רב ששת shows this is wrong: שבת forbids only מלאכת מחשבת, purposeful creative work. Simply collecting food into a pile or a handful is not that kind of work, so it can be the finishing point for מעשר and still be permitted on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Planned, purposeful, creative labor, the only kind the Torah forbids on שבת
The Torah forbade
Here too, the same applies
Rather, what must you say? (introduces the only possible explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: What finishes produce for מעשר is a different question from what counts as forbidden labor on שבת. שבת forbids only מלאכת מחשבת, so gathering into a pile or a handful is not forbidden, even though it fixes the obligation of מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying that שבת is more lenient than מעשר in general. The point is that the two areas use different standards. מעשר asks whether the produce is finished. שבת asks whether a creative labor was done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the challenge from step 17. It also confirms the reading from step 16: רבי אלעזר's 'וכן לשבת' refers to rubbing wheat and blowing away the chaff, not to gathering barley in one's hand.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say (about piling)?
phrases.notes: Asks why piling is פטור on שבת

phrases.english: The Torah forbade only planned, creative labor;
here too (with gathering peeled barley):
the Torah forbade only planned, creative labor.
phrases.notes: So gathering into the hand is not a forbidden labor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the counter-example in step 18 and applies that reason to the barley case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Something can be 'finished' for מעשר without being a forbidden labor on שבת, because שבת forbids only מלאכת מחשבת. The קשיא of רבי אבא בר ממל is resolved.

steps.title: How may one rub the grain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the permitted way to rub (מולל) grain kernels to remove the husk.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one rub the grain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new practical question. This short line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know that רבי אלעזר applied the rule to rubbing wheat and blowing the chaff on שבת. This question is about how one may rub grain on יום טוב, the topic of this מסכת. The answers that follow require a changed, unusual way of rubbing.

keyTerms.meaning: How? In what manner?
Rubs grain kernels between the fingers to remove the husk

phrases.english: How does one rub (the grain)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory behind רבי אלעזר's rule to how the permitted rubbing is actually done.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What way of rubbing grain counts as a permitted change from the normal way of working?

steps.title: אביי: Rub with one finger against one finger
steps.stepSummary: אביי, quoting רב יוסף, says one may rub the grain only between one finger and one other finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said in the name of רב יוסף: one finger against one finger.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. Rub using only one finger against one other finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally people rub grain using the whole hand. Using just two fingers is a clear change (שינוי), and that change is what makes it permitted. This is the strictest view, allowing only a very small change in method.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
One (finger) against one (finger)

phrases.english: Abaye said in the name of Rav Yosef:
One (finger) against one (finger).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rubbing is permitted only between one finger and one other finger.

steps.title: רב אויא: One finger against two
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא, also quoting רב יוסף, reports a broader version. One may rub with one finger against two fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אויא said in the name of רב יוסף: one finger against two.
steps.whatsHappening: A second student reports רב יוסף's ruling differently and allows a little more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the thumb against two fingers is still not the normal whole-hand way of rubbing. So רב אויא holds it still counts as a change. The two students disagree only about how much of the hand may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: One (finger) against two (fingers)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַוְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Avya said in the name of Rav Yosef:
One (finger) against two (fingers).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַוְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, more lenient report of רב יוסף's answer than אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rubbing is permitted with one finger against two fingers.

steps.title: רבא: Since he changes the method, even one finger against all
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that because any changed method is enough, one may even rub with one finger against all the other fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since he is doing it differently, he may even use one finger against all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the most lenient answer. Any change from the normal way is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is the שינוי itself. Once the person is not rubbing in the usual way, it no longer matters how many fingers he uses. So even the thumb against all four fingers is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he changes (the usual method)
Against all of them (all the fingers)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on rubbing grain: one against one (אביי), one against two (רב אויא), and one against all (רבא). All three agree that some שינוי from the normal way is required.

phrases.english: Rava said: Since he changes (the method) —
even one (finger) against all of them is also (permitted).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond both reports of רב יוסף and gives a broad reason: any change permits it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the method is changed, even one finger against all the others is permitted.

steps.title: How may one blow away the chaff?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the permitted way to blow (מנפח) the chaff off the rubbed grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one blow (away the chaff)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second practical question, about the next stage after rubbing. This line sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing away chaff is a form of winnowing, which is normally a forbidden labor. So, just like rubbing, it needs a permitted, changed method.

keyTerms.meaning: Blows on the grain to separate the chaff

phrases.english: How does one blow (away the chaff)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the rubbing question with a parallel question about blowing away the chaff.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What way of blowing away chaff is permitted?

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה in the name of רב begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה, quoting רב, starts to explain how one blows. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: One blows…
steps.whatsHappening: רב's answer about blowing begins here. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is not yet stated on this amud. We should expect another change from the usual way of winnowing, similar to the changed method of rubbing.

keyTerms.meaning: רב said (the source of the ruling)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
One blows…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet complete; רב's method of blowing continues on the next amud.
